mig_27k: The MiG-27K was Mikoyan's fully upgraded version of the swing-wing MiG-27 strike jet, built around the Kayra-23 laser-optical sight so it could use laser- and TV-guided weapons; its cost led the Soviet Air Force to halve the order and fill the rest with the cheaper MiG-27M. It is at home in both game modes: in air battles it can wipe out a base and still carry a complete air-to-air missile fit, with the same strong low-level performance as the MiG-27M, while in mixed battles its sight and guided arsenal make precise ground strikes easy. It arrived with the "Winged Lions" update.
mig_27m: The MiG-27M was the budget half of the late MiG-27 upgrade: it made do with Su-17-derived targeting gear instead of the costly Kayra-23 of the MiG-27K, yet could still employ laser- and TV-guided weapons, and it served the USSR and export users in the 1980s. R-13M1 and R-60M missiles, a good stock of large countermeasures and a MiG-23BN-based airframe let it defend itself, but its real job is precision attack. It is the first aircraft on the Soviet bomber line with guided weapons, and with those plus the six-barrel GSh-6-30 cannon it is a dependable mixed-battle striker. It came in Update "Direct Hit".
mig_29_9_12: Mikoyan's light frontline fighter was conceived in the 1970s to work alongside the larger Su-27 and replace the MiG-23; it first flew in October 1977, and the 9-12 production model reached units in 1983, designed to be fast, agile and easy to maintain from rough airfields, though short on range. Quick, nimble and with a decent radar and helmet sight for its short- and medium-range missiles, it is held back by older missiles than later Fulcrums carry, notably R-60Ms that flares fool easily, and by having little to use on ground targets. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
mig_29_9_12_germany: East Germany bought 24 export-standard MiG-29 9-12A fighters in the 1980s, and after reunification the Luftwaffe kept them for more than a decade; a 1994 exercise against USAF F-16s at Aviano showed NATO how badly it had underrated the type, and in 2003 22 of them went to Poland for one euro apiece. For German pilots it is the first step into fourth-generation jets after the MiG-23MLA, adding the hard-hitting R-27ER1 and a helmet sight that allows its all-aspect heat-seekers to be fired well off the nose. It came with Update 2.25 "Sky Guardians".
mig_29_9_12_sniper: Romania's MiG-29 Sniper was an upgrade programme that would have given its Fulcrums Western avionics, including colour multifunction displays, a new HUD and an Elisra SPS-20(V) radar warning receiver, while keeping Soviet weapons; it was cancelled in favour of the MiG-21 LanceR. A premium pack in the Italian tree since the "Leviathans" update, it keeps the usual Fulcrum flaws: a N019E radar weaker than NATO equivalents and an airframe that bleeds energy against F-15s and F-16s. Its digital RWR is a real asset, naming radar types and warning of tracks and launches, and it fights with R-27ERs at range and R-60Ms plus a helmet sight up close.
mig_29_9_12b_hungary: Hungary received 28 MiG-29s of the 9-12B standard in 1993 as part of Russia's debt settlement, a big step up from its worn MiG-23MFs; after joining NATO in 1999 it moved to the Gripen and retired its last Fulcrum in December 2010. Found in the Hungarian part of the Italian tree, it gives players a differently flying option to the F-16A ADF. The long-reaching R-27ER1 and off-boresight shots with all-aspect IR missiles through a helmet sight are the big gains over the MiG-23MF before it. It arrived in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
mig_29_9_12g: After reunification the Luftwaffe kept its ex-East German MiG-29s, which had outperformed most NATO fighters in testing, and upgraded them as the MiG-29G with Western avionics and NATO-compatible communications and navigation. In the game it keeps the familiar feel of the 9-12 but gains R-27ET1 and R-73E missiles. Next to the MiG-29SMT it gives up the newer radar, extra fuel and countermeasures and the guided ground weapons, and in return avoids that version's heavy weight, which makes it a lighter, more agile sidegrade. It was introduced in the "Kings of Battle" update.
mig_29_9_13: Shaped by Soviet lessons that agile fighters still mattered, Mikoyan's Fulcrum first flew in October 1977 with twin engines, a strong radar and a helmet-mounted sight for close combat; the 9-13 entered production in 1986 with a larger fuel bulge behind the cockpit and reshaped wingtips. When added in Update "Apex Predators" it became the Soviet tree's first fourth-generation fighter, and it plays almost exactly like the 9-12. Its jump over the MiG-23 is large: the radar is a genuine pulse-Doppler set, the R-27ER ranks among the strongest radar-guided missiles, and the helmet sight lets R-60M and R-27T shots go well off the nose.
mig_29kr_9_41r: The carrier-based MiG-29K, derived from the MiG-29M, first landed on the carrier now called Admiral Kuznetsov in 1989 but was shelved after the Soviet collapse; revived by an Indian order, it returned for the Russian Navy, which contracted 20 single-seat MiG-29KRs in 2012 and used them against targets in Syria in 2016. A larger wing and more powerful engines set it apart from the MiG-29M. It relies on R-77s and R-73s against aircraft, with no R-27 option, while Kh-31A/P and TV-guided Kh-29 missiles give it real punch against ground targets, so it suits air and mixed battles alike. It was added in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
mig_29m_9_15: A deep redesign of the Fulcrum begun in the mid-1980s, the MiG-29M gained a reworked airframe with more fuel, fly-by-wire controls and the N010 Zhuk radar, opening up R-77 missiles and precision strike weapons; six prototypes flew, but early-1990s budget cuts stopped production, and the design fed into the MiG-29K and MiG-35. Its headline feature is room for eight R-77s, a big step beyond the 9-13 and SMT, backed by up to four TV-guided Kh-29TDs for strikes. RD-33K engines claw back some of the added weight, but a small flare supply and no targeting pod hold it back. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
mig_29n: Malaysia ordered 18 MiG-29s in 1994, took delivery in 1995 and later upgraded them locally towards the 9.12SD standard with in-flight refuelling, a better radar and RVV-AE missiles; they served until 2017, when the Su-30MKM replaced them. In the Japanese tree its powerful engines make it fast and nimble, and RVV-AE active radar missiles give an otherwise early Fulcrum real reach. The trade-offs are old avionics and a ground-attack fit of rockets, napalm and unguided bombs that does little against armour. It came in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
mig_29smt_9_19: With Russia's next-generation fighter programmes stalled for lack of money, RSK MiG revived its 1990s MiG-29SMT modernisation as a cheaper answer to late F-16s and the new European canard fighters; the 9-19 standard was finalised in 2006 and serves with Russia, Algeria and Syria. R-77 active radar missiles, better radar and avionics, and a broad set of guided air-to-ground weapons make it far deadlier than the MiG-29 (9-13), although it handles noticeably worse. It was added in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila".
mig_35: A "4++ generation" development of the MiG-29M and MiG-29K, the MiG-35 adds an AESA radar, a new helmet display and more guided strike weapons; it first flew in January 2017, and Russia took its first two production jets in 2019. In the game it climbs fast, is quick high up and turns at subsonic speed as sharply as any Fulcrum, carrying R-77-1 and R-73 missiles cued by that radar and helmet sight for short- and medium-range fights. Kh-38ML/MT missiles and guided bombs make it dangerous in mixed battles, but fuel is tight and has to be watched. It came in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mig_3_series_1_15: Designed by Mikoyan-Gurevich as a high-altitude interceptor, the MiG-3 could outpace the Bf 109 at around 6,000 m, though its AM-35A engine left it slower near sea level. In the game it is one of the first fighters able to reach high-flying bombers, and it works best climbing early and diving on targets below rather than turning, as its controls are stiff and it is less agile than its rivals. Its nose guns, one 12.7 mm and two 7.62 mm, are easy to aim without convergence settings but lack punch, so the engine, pilot and fuel tanks are the targets to aim for. It was added in Update 1.31.
mig_3_series_1_15_bk_pod: This MiG-3-15 variant differs from the standard aircraft only in two extra non-synchronised 12.7 mm Berezin UB guns, giving it three UBs and two 7.62 mm ShKAS behind a 1,200 hp Mikulin AM-35A. Its three UBs are the largest such battery used as main armament on any aircraft in the game; the gun outpaces the American M2 Browning in rate of fire and muzzle velocity, and short bursts at wings or engines bring down light fighters, though bombers soak up hits better. Like the base MiG-3 it is an energy fighter suited to boom-and-zoom, quite unlike the I-16 line before it. It arrived in Update 1.37.
mig_3_series_34: An experimental MiG-3 variant meant to fix the series' weak firepower, the MiG-3-34 came from a high-altitude design that struggled in service with poor build quality and oxygen supply, and in 1941 it met agile Bf 109s instead of bombers before Yak and LaGG fighters replaced it. Above 4,000 m its engine reaches full power, and that is where it belongs: hunting bombers and fighting on speed and acceleration in the manner of the I-185 and I-225, rather than turning or trading fire with Spitfires and Bf 109s, which outclass it in agility and firepower. It arrived in Update 1.41.
mirage_2000_5eg_mk2_greece: Greece ordered 40 Mirage 2000s in 1985 and in the early 2000s upgraded part of the fleet and bought 15 more to the 2000-5 Mk.2 standard, with RDY-2 radar, modern avionics and MICA missiles; the Rafale is now replacing them. Functionally a copy of the French Mirage 2000-5F, it pairs MICA-EM missiles at medium range with R550 Magic 2s for close fights, while its delta wing and strong engine make it agile and quick, though it bleeds speed in long turning fights. Against ground targets it has nothing but anti-radiation missiles. It was added to the Israeli tree in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mirage_2000_5ei: Taiwan's air force, unable to buy F-4s or F-16s from the US in the 1980s to replace ageing F-104s and F-5s, turned to France and received Mirage 2000-5Ei fighters from 1997 with ground-attack capability removed; the deal helped push Washington into selling F-16s from 1998. In the Chinese tree it is essentially a single-seat Mirage 2000-5F without strike weapons. Outranged by opponents such as the F-15E and the J-10A it faced in reality, it is at its best cleaning up the last enemy jets late in a match with its MICA-EM missiles and good electronics. It arrived in Update "Firebirds".
mirage_2000_5f: Dassault's Mirage 2000-5F, first flown in 1991, brought upgraded avionics and weapons to the Mirage 2000 line and flew both air-to-air and ground-attack sorties over Kosovo in 1999. In the game it is above all an air-superiority jet: agile enough to gain the upper hand in a turning fight, it uses the Thales RDY radar to find and track several targets quickly and finishes them at close range with the infrared-guided Matra Magic 2. It came to the game in the "La Royale" update.
mirage_2000c_s4: Dassault's Mirage 2000 first flew in 1978 after the AFVG and Mirage G projects failed, and the C ("Chasseur") version long served as France's main interceptor. The C-S4 arrived in Update "Air Superiority" as a reward from the 2023 Winter Extreme event and is nearly identical to the tech-tree C-S5, but has fewer countermeasures and no missile approach warning. In practice the two fly the same way: its performance lets it decide when to fight, with Super 530D radar missiles for longer shots and all-aspect R.550 Magic 2s up close.
mirage_2000c_s5: The penultimate Mirage 2000C standard added the uprated M53-P2 engine, an Eclair chaff and flare dispenser and the improved RDI radar for the Super 530D missile, bringing it level with contemporary MiG-29s and F-16s. Its light airframe and strong engine are the selling points: it accelerates hard, reaches high speeds and pulls a high angle of attack, and although the delta sheds energy at low speed it regains it quickly. It carries fewer missiles and bombs than rivals, and the 530D trails late AIM-7s and R-27s at range, so it does best kept low, using the IRCCM-equipped Magic 2 inside about 3 km. It arrived in Update "Drone Age".
mirage_2000d_r1: Descended from the nuclear-strike Mirage 2000N by way of the 2000D, the D-R1 is a two-seat ground-attack Mirage with improved countermeasures, ECM and RWR, plus AS-30L missiles, laser-guided bombs and a targeting pod. Its guided weapons are accurate but few, two GBU-12s and two AS-30Ls alongside a pair of Magic 2s, so it fits ground battles best, bombing from altitude first and then using the AS-30L, whose HE warhead is better spent on distant SPAA than on tanks. Despite the extra weight, the 2000C-family engine gives brisk low-speed acceleration and plenty of top speed, though it drinks fuel. It arrived in Update "Apex Predators".
mirage_2000d_rmv: Dassault's mid-life renovation programme, launched in 2015, gave the strike Mirage new avionics and a wider range of weapons, with upgraded aircraft reaching units from 2022 and 55 planned to keep the type flying into the 2030s. Its game role is unchanged from the D-R1, a strike specialist that struggles against aircraft, but the weapon list grows: the DAMOCLES pod and GBU-48, GBU-49 and GBU-50 bombs with both satellite and laser guidance join the older stores. It came in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
mirage_3c: The first production Mirage III, the IIIC was a delta-wing interceptor and dogfighter with an afterburning Atar 09B, DEFA 30 mm cannons and, at first, AIM-9B Sidewinders; 95 were built and it served until 1988. Its game kit follows the usual French delta pattern of 30 mm cannon, a strong engine and Magic 1 heat-seekers, with R530E radar missiles for medium range, though the radar is only really useful at high altitude. Without flares and with mediocre acceleration, it should avoid being tied up near several enemies, keeping its speed high and saving Magic 1s for shots inside about 2 km. It arrived in Update "Starfighters".
mirage_3cj: The Shahak was Israel's Mirage IIICJ and its first Mach 2 fighter, the main air superiority aircraft through the Six-Day and Yom Kippur wars, where pilots often trusted the DEFA cannons over unreliable missiles; 72 served before the Kfir and F-4 took over. Its flight model is close to the French Mirage IIIC, but American AIM-9Ds replace the Magic 1s. Speed is its main defence, since it carries no countermeasures and accelerates sluggishly at low speed, and while it turns sharply and pulls a high angle of attack, it bleeds energy doing so. It came with the "Winged Lions" update.
mirage_3e: Built as a more multirole partner to the interceptor Mirage IIIC, the IIIE added a British pulse-Doppler navigation radar under the cockpit, more fuel, a newer ATAR 09 engine and better avionics; with 192 built for the French Air Force, it was the most produced Mirage III by 1971. Where the IIIC is a pure interceptor, the IIIE can also attack ground targets, with a ballistic computer aiding gun, rocket and bomb runs. It adds an RWR and countermeasures too, and its revised Atar 9 answers the throttle far faster while giving slightly more thrust. It arrived in Update "Ixwa Strike".
mirage_3s_c70_switzerland: Switzerland chose the Mirage IIIC as its first supersonic fighter and built it under licence as the Mirage IIIS, though funding cut production from 100 to 54; from 1988 the fleet gained canards (C.70 stands for "canard wing at 70%") and new avionics, and most retired in 1999. In the German tree the Swiss upgrades give it an edge over the French IIIC in avionics and missiles, notably the semi-active AIM-26 and a licence-built AIM-9E, and besides the SEPR844 rocket booster it can use new JATO rockets. Against that, it sheds speed heavily in turns and has no air-to-ground armament. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
mirage_4000: Dassault's private-venture Mirage 4000, essentially a twin-engined, canard-equipped Mirage 2000 scaled up to rival the F-15, found no buyer: France judged it too expensive and export prospects fell through, so the single prototype ended up in a Paris museum in 1992, its lessons passing to the Rafale. Few French aircraft are as versatile: four Super 530Ds and a strong radar handle longer-range work, as many as eight Magic 2s cover the close fights it already excels in, and the ATLIS pod with laser-guided bombs and missiles makes it a serious attacker. It came in Update "Air Superiority" and will feel familiar to Mirage 2000 pilots.
mirage_5ba: Belgium ordered Mirage 5s in 1968 to replace its F-84F and RF-84F jets, with 54 of the planned 88 being Mirage 5BA fighters fitted with American electronics; after the Cold War, Chile bought 20 of them, naming them Elkan. In the game its one difference from France's own Mirage 5F is a countermeasure dispenser. Otherwise it is a nimble fighter whose missiles are effective but few, with a modest cannon ammunition supply and no guided air-to-ground weapons. It came in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
mirage_5f: The Mirage 5 was a stripped-down Mirage III requested by Israel, trading radar and avionics for extra fuel; France's 1967 arms embargo blocked delivery of the 50 ordered, and Israel, after taking a refund, built its own copy, the Nesher, from blueprints obtained through espionage. It shares its airframe with the Nesher but swaps Shafrir 2s for AIM-9Bs and Magic 1s. With no radar, no countermeasures and just two short-range missiles, it does best as a fast base bomber that avoids enemies carrying all-aspect missiles and uses its speed and brief dogfighting ability to catch the unwary. It came in the "Winged Lions" update.
mirage_f1c: Begun by Dassault as a private venture to replace the Mirage III and 5, the swept-wing Mirage F1 with its Atar 9K-50 first flew in late 1966 and joined the French Air Force in March 1974, later seeing action over Chad and in the Gulf War. Its handling is unremarkable: it holds high g at speed and keeps its energy well but dislikes high angles of attack. Apart from two flare-resistant IRCCM Magic 2s its missiles are ordinary, so it works best in support, taking long-range shots at high-flying targets, as its radar struggles to find aircraft down low. It arrived in Update "Wind of Change".
mirage_f1c_200: The F1C-200 is the Mirage F1C fitted with an in-flight refuelling probe, which added 7 cm to the fuselage, for long expeditionary deployments; in the early 1980s these aircraft escorted Jaguars striking insurgents in Chad. In the game it is flown just like the F1C, as a support fighter rather than a frontline brawler, since it cannot match the MiG-21bis and MiG-23s up close or the F-4J/S and F-14A at long range. Its pair of IRCCM Magic 2s are excellent, its other missiles are mediocre but reach far, especially at altitude, and it can flatten a whole base while staying useful in the air. It arrived in Update "Apex Predators".
mirage_f1cg_greece: Greece bought 40 single-seat Mirage F1CGs, a version with its own armament fit, to replace its F-102As; ordered in 1974 and delivered from 1975, they spent their careers in mock dogfights with Turkish jets, with losses on both sides, before the last 27 were retired in June 2003. In the Israeli tree it has no Magic 2 or other Matra missiles, but it meets far less modern opposition than the French F1s do. That makes its good speed, reasonable agility and generous countermeasure supply count for more. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mirage_f1ct: When the Mirage 2000 began taking over French fighter duties, surplus Mirage F1Cs were converted from 1988 into the F1CT ground-attack jet to replace old Mirage IIIEs and 5s: it gained the F1CR's avionics and Cyrano IVM-R radar, a laser rangefinder under the nose, a new RWR and larger chaff and flare dispensers, while keeping the fighter's air-to-air weapons. Although it sits in the attacker line, its superior RWR makes it the strongest F1 in air combat, and a bigger bomb load gives it the edge against ground targets too. Reached through the shorter attacker line, it is also the quickest F1 to obtain; it arrived in Update "Danger Zone".
mirage_milan: The Milan was a Mirage III derivative begun in 1968 for Switzerland, pairing the airframe with the Jaguar's weapon systems and retractable nose "whiskers" that shortened take-off and added lift; it first flew in May 1970, but the Swiss bought F-5s instead. A big strike payload, strong engine and ballistic computer make it more attacker than fighter in the game. It lacks the Magic 1, R530 and countermeasures of the Mirage IIIC/E and 5F, so in the air it relies on speed and short-ranged AIM-9Bs fired at unaware targets within 2 km. Added in Update "Danger Zone", it left sale in 2023, returning only briefly for Bastille Day events.
morko_morane: Finland rebuilt its Morane-Saulnier M.S.406 fighters with captured Soviet Klimov VK-105P engines and heavier armament, but the conversions were slow and the first Mörkö-Morane only arrived in 1944, in time to give a reasonable account of itself in the Continuation War. Compared with the French M.S.406C1 it has over 300 hp more, a rounder cowling and a Bf 109-style oil cooler, which turns it into a strong energy fighter. The nose weapon is either a 12.7 mm Berezin UB or a 20 mm MG 151 with mine shells, light but adequate for the opposition it meets. It is a low-tier Swedish premium added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
mosquito_b_mk16: Developed from 1943 as an improved Mosquito bomber, the B Mk XVI gained a two-stage supercharger, cabin pressurisation and a bomb bay enlarged for the 4,000 lb "Cookie"; 245 were built, counting the Canadian Mk XX, and they flew until the war's end. In the game it exists to carry bombs, and its speed lets it reach bases quickly and strike ground targets accurately. It has no guns at all, though, so anything fast enough to catch it can shoot it down unopposed. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
mosquito_f_mk2_norway: The F.Mk.II was the rare daytime version of the first Mosquito fighter, built in very small numbers mainly to catch German high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft; Norway's 333rd Squadron, formed in May 1943 and flying in RAF markings, used it among other Mosquitos and lost many crews that summer. In the Swedish tree it is a pure gun fighter with no ordnance and no radar, about 800 kg lighter than the NF.Mk.II and therefore a little more nimble. Like other early Mosquitos it is quick and heavily armed but fragile and poor in a turning fight. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
mosquito_fb_mk18: Nicknamed Tsetse, the FB Mk XVIII swapped the FB Mk VI's Hispano cannons for a single 57 mm Molins gun with a 25-round autoloader and added armour underneath, to hunt U-boats; only 18 were built, yet from 1944 they sank several submarines and surface ships. That big gun fires an armour-piercing shell with ample penetration, so it deals with tanks as readily as it did with boats. Against aircraft it is poor: the 57 mm only has AP rounds that pass straight through, the four 7.7 mm guns are weak and the armour costs agility, so it is a ground-attack machine. It arrived in Update 1.39.
mosquito_fb_mk26_china: The FB Mk 26 was a Canadian upgrade of the Mosquito FB Mk VI with Packard Merlin 225 engines, and in 1948 the Republic of China bought 205 Mosquitoes from Canada, including this model; the humid climate made them hard to maintain, and they were dismantled in 1950 after five were lost fighting the Communists. In the Chinese tree it is a quick multirole aircraft with heavy guns and a strong bomb load. It is fragile, however, and a single-engined fighter will usually beat it in a turning fight. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
mosquito_fb_mk6: The FB Mk VI was the fighter-bomber version of de Havilland's mostly wooden Mosquito, the "Wooden Wonder", carrying four 20 mm Hispanos and four .303 Brownings in the nose plus bombs, and it flew precision raids such as the attack on a Gestapo headquarters. Its nose battery tears enemy aircraft apart, and bombs and rockets let it contribute against ground targets as well. As a twin-engined design it is out-turned by true fighters, more so when loaded, and the wooden airframe catches fire easily, so it should pick its moments rather than seek a fight. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
mosquito_fb_mk6_ash_norway: Some Mosquito FB Mk VIs gave up their four machine guns for an AI Mk XV ASH ship-search radar, the set squeezed into the nose with its antennas in the wing. Norway's 333rd Squadron rebuilt around the FB Mk VI after heavy losses, flying reconnaissance and anti-ship missions to the end of the war, and kept its aircraft until jets replaced them in 1952. In the Swedish tree it plays almost exactly like the standard FB Mk VI: fast, well armed and carrying a good payload, but fragile and outmatched by single-engined fighters. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
mosquito_fb_mk6_norway: The FB Mk VI, the Mosquito's strike version, grew out of the F Mk II with underwing weapon mounts, an extra fuel tank and a strengthened wing; it first flew in June 1942 and, at 2,140 built, was the most numerous variant. It became the mainstay of Norway's 333rd Squadron for reconnaissance and anti-shipping work for the rest of the war, then went home with the squadron in late 1945 and flew until 1952. In the Swedish tree it is a fast multirole with powerful guns and a good bomb load, but it is easily damaged and loses dogfights to single-engined fighters. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
mosquito_j30_sweden: Sweden's J30 was the Mosquito NF.Mk.XIX, a 1944 night fighter with Merlin 25 engines and British or American radar, of which 280 were built; 60 ex-RAF examples were bought in 1948 and flew with the three squadrons of the F1 wing, told apart by white, blue and yellow spinners, until the Venom replaced them in 1954. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season 22, "The Elusive Musketeer". Compared with the NF.Mk.II it has a newer radar but more weight, which hurts its handling; beyond that it is a typical Mosquito, fast and hard-hitting but fragile and out-turned by single-engined fighters.
mosquito_nf_mk2: Born from Geoffrey de Havilland's idea of a fast wooden aircraft and first flown in November 1940, the Mosquito was built in 7,780 examples and used by 22 countries; the NF.Mk.II was its first night fighter, a gun-armed F.Mk.II with AI Mk.IV radar, and 466 were made. In the game it carries no bombs or rockets, and the weight saved makes it handle better than most Mosquitos. In other respects it matches the FB.Mk.VI, with plenty of speed and a heavy nose armament but little resilience and limited agility. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
mosquito_tr_mk33: The Sea Mosquito answered a 1944 Royal Navy call for a carrier-capable twin: after an FB Mk VI fitted with a tail hook was trialled aboard HMS Indefatigable, the TR.Mk.33 entered production in late 1945 with ASH radar and torpedo capability. Fifty were built, reaching units in 1946 and serving quietly until 1952. In the game it is close to the Norwegian FB Mk VI ASH, only heavier and able to drop torpedoes, and it shares the usual Mosquito traits: fast, well armed and with a useful payload, but easily damaged and no match for single-engined fighters in a dogfight. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
ms_405c1: Morane-Saulnier's M.S.405C1 was the pre-production forerunner of the M.S.406, armed with a 20 mm Hispano 404 firing through the propeller hub and two 7.5 mm MAC 1934 wing guns; it beat several rival designs in 1937 trials, but as a test aircraft it never fought. In the game it turns well by monoplane standards, though many biplanes turn tighter, and its high speed limit of roughly 750 km/h lets it switch between turning fights and boom-and-zoom. With no armour at all, it does not take damage well. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
ms_406c1: The production development of the M.S.405, the M.S.406C1 used a Hispano-Suiza 12Y-31 engine rated for lower altitude and entered French service in May 1938; 1,176 were built, and though easy for inexperienced pilots, it was outclassed by the Bf 109 E, serving with France and Finland. In the game it is nimble for a monoplane but still out-turned by many biplanes. It climbs worse than the M.S.405C1, which makes hit-and-run attacks harder despite a high speed limit of about 750 km/h, and the lack of armour leaves it vulnerable. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
ms_410c1: Meant to improve on the M.S.406 with a new wing, stronger armament and a fixed radiator, the M.S.410 entered production too close to France's surrender in June 1940 to serve with the French Air Force, though some were built under German oversight in Vichy France. In the game it shares the traits of other French fighters at its rank: agile but slow and fragile, with modest firepower. Its decent climb helps it keep the initiative against slower opponents, as many German and American fighters can outrun it, and its 20 mm ammunition is best saved for fighters rather than bombers. It came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
n1k1_ja: Kawanishi, a floatplane specialist, produced its first land-based fighter by giving the N1K1 floatplane design conventional landing gear and swapping its Kasei 13 for the more powerful Nakajima Homare; the resulting Shiden proved a dangerous opponent for Allied pilots. Opening the N1K land-fighter line in the game, it handles best at roughly 350-450 km/h, where it out-turns nearly everything bar some Japanese and British types, and its heavy armament makes short work of bombers. It is short on speed and climb and poor at diving attacks, so faster, nimble enemies are best avoided or drawn into turning at speed. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
n1k1_kyuofu: Kawanishi's Kyōfū was a floatplane fighter designed in 1940 to support offensives far from airfields, but by its 1943 service debut Japan was on the defensive, and it saw only limited action against stronger Allied fighters; it did lead to the land-based Shiden. Armed with two 20 mm cannon and two 7.7 mm guns and reaching 489 km/h, it outperforms the A6M2-N in the game, with more cannon ammunition and self-sealing tanks. The floats still drag on performance, so careless energy management makes it an easy target and it is not a forgiving aircraft for beginners. It arrived in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
n1k2_j: The Shiden Kai fixed most of the N1K1-J's faults: a low wing allowed shorter landing gear, the fuselage and tail were reworked, and it came out 250 kg lighter, faster and simpler to build, though the Homare engine stayed troublesome. Hard to master, it beats most piston fighters and out-turns the much faster early jets, but other superprops generally outperform it, so mid-speed handling is its key asset. For ground battles it takes two 250 kg bombs or Type 5 rockets, and AP-belted 20 mm cannons can kill soft targets and medium tanks from above. It has been part of the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
n1k2_jko: The N1K2-Ja was a small revision of the Shiden Kai that let it carry four 60 kg or two 250 kg bombs and trimmed 13% off the fin's leading edge, striking a better balance between agility and stability. In play it matches the N1K2-J: tricky to master and best at medium speed, nimbler but far slower than early jets, and stronger than most piston fighters yet usually bettered by other superprops. For ground battles it brings 250 kg bombs or Type 5 rockets, and an APHE belt for the four 20 mm cannons can destroy soft targets and medium armour from above. It dates from the open beta, before Update 1.27.
nc_223_3: A development of the Farman F.220 family, the N.C.223.3 resembled the F.222.2 but had twin fins for steadier yaw control, Hispano-Suiza 12Y-29 engines and 20 mm Hispano cannons in its dorsal and ventral defensive positions; after France fell in 1940 the bombers went to North Africa as transports. In the game it is slow and survives by flying high, but it carries 52 x 50 kg bombs, enough for a base, or an airfield with help from other bombers. The airframe is tough and the rear cannons hit hard, though they leave several blind spots, notably around the tail. It came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
nesher: Israel's Nesher was a covert local copy of the Mirage 5, built from 1969 to sidestep the French embargo, with Israeli avionics and Shafrir 2 and AIM-9D missiles; it fought well in 1973, and refurbished examples later flew in Argentina as the Dagger until 2015. It handles like other early Mirages, fast and agile only while it keeps its speed, and without flares it needs to stay near Mach 1 to survive. Its two DEFA 30 mm cannons are easy to aim and the AIM-9G is its best missile; it can level a base, but with no ballistic computer it is poor at close air support. It arrived in Update "Winged Lions".
nf_5a_netherlands: The NF-5A was the Dutch version of the Canadair CF-5A, a licence-built F-5 with taller nose gear, improved navigation and modified engines; the Netherlands took 105 single- and two-seat aircraft between 1969 and 1972 to replace F-84Fs and T-33s, and after retiring them in 1991 sold them to Turkey, Greece and Venezuela. Placed in the French tree, it flies much like the American F-5A, nimble and tough but slow. The main difference is its missiles: AIM-9J and AIM-9N rather than the AIM-9E. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
nimrod_mk1: Hawker's Nimrod was a carrier-based adaptation of the Fury biplane, first built privately in 1930 under the name "Norn" and replacing the Fairey Flycatcher in Fleet Air Arm squadrons from 1932, armed with two .303 Vickers guns and up to 80 lb of bombs. In the game it is slow, which leaves it exposed to faster fighters, but it climbs better than most biplanes and turns very well. Like the Fury and the later Nimrod, its two 7.7 mm guns lack punch, and the I-15 and Ki-10 can turn inside it, the I-15 outgunning it as well. It dates back to the open beta, before Update 1.27.
nimrod_mk2: From 1934 the Nimrod Mk II replaced the Mk I on the production line, bringing an arrestor hook, slightly swept wings, larger tail surfaces and a 608 hp Kestrel V; only 30 were built, and they left frontline service for the Sea Gladiator and Skua before the war. Its edge over the Mk I lies in the swept wing and extra power, giving fine climb, turn and roll rates in a forgiving package that suits newcomers, though its two 7.7 mm Vickers guns are weak. The open cockpit's clear view also makes it a good first aircraft for Simulator Battles. It has been available since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
o3u_1: The O3U-1 was a 1930 US Navy observation seaplane that refined the O2U with better engine performance, equipment and aerodynamics; 289 O3Us of all versions were built up to 1936, and China bought 21 for bombing raids in the Second Sino-Japanese War. It joined the game in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons" as a ship-launched scout. With no forward guns, a single 7.7 mm Lewis gun in the rear and two 100 lb bombs, it can pick off small coastal craft that have little means of firing back, but it is slow and flimsy, so better-armed ships bring it down easily.
oh_58d: Bell's Kiowa grew from the commercial 206A, which won a re-run US Army light observation contest in 1967; the OH-58D Kiowa Warrior, first flown in 1983, added a four-blade rotor, more power, a new cockpit and the distinctive sight above the rotor mast, and it served in Iraq and Afghanistan before retiring by 2020. In the game this small, lively helicopter carries a lot: rocket pods, Hellfire II missiles and a fast-firing 30 mm LR30 grenade launcher. Stingers, an RWR, countermeasures and its compact size help it in air combat, but with no armour at all it relies on alertness and careful flying. It arrived in Update "Sons of Attila".
oh_58d_china: Taiwan's army bought 39 OH-58D Kiowa Warriors from the US, 26 in 1992 alongside its AH-1Ws and 13 more in 1999 assembled locally by AIDC, and with up to 12 years of spare parts stocked it expects to keep them flying for some time. In the Chinese tree it matches the American version except that it cannot mount the 30 mm grenade launcher or the 7.62 mm Minigun. Its mast-mounted sight lets it watch from behind trees and ridges, four AGM-114K Hellfire IIs deal easily with ground vehicles, and its small size, Stingers and countermeasure pods partly make up for the absence of armour. It came with Update "Sons of Attila".
os2u_1: Vought-Sikorsky's Kingfisher was a catapult-launched observation floatplane for US Navy cruisers and battleships; its spot-welded, smooth-skinned fuselage cut drag, and despite modest performance it replaced the Curtiss SOC Seagull after production began in 1940. Neither fast nor well armed, it should leave enemy fighters alone and look for undefended ground targets, but it does its original job well as a scout in naval battles. An open-beta original, it was taken out of the research tree in Update 1.57 "Battle March", later returned via the American naval tree, and since "Winged Lions" can also be launched from some US ships.
os2u_3: The most produced Kingfisher, with 1,000 built from 1941, the OS2U-3 added two self-sealing wing tanks for more range and better pilot armour, and it was the only version exported, reaching users from Uruguay to Australia and even the Soviet cruiser Murmansk. With one forward 7.62 mm gun, another for the gunner and lacklustre performance, it is easy prey for fighters. As a naval scout it shines: it spots targets from afar, can set down on the water when its job is done or AA gets close, and climbs faster than the OS2U-1. Removed in Update 1.57, it later returned via the naval tree.
osprey_mk4: A navalised version of the Hawker Hart biplane with a Kestrel II engine and a 7.7 mm gun for each crew member, the Osprey served from 1932 to 1944 as a reconnaissance aircraft from ships and shore bases, and was also sold to Sweden for the seaplane cruiser HSwMS Gotland, to Portugal and to Republican Spain. In the game it flies from the cruisers HMNZS Leander and HMS Kent. Slow and lightly armed but nimble, it is well suited to laying protective smoke screens around its ship, though without bombs or heavier guns it cannot attack vessels. It arrived in Update "Winged Lions".
p-26a_33: Boeing's P-26 "Peashooter", begun as a company-funded project in 1931, was a monoplane fighter ordered by the US Army Air Corps and meant to outpace and out-turn the biplanes then in service. The 1932 prototypes landed so fast that their undercarriage could fail, so later aircraft gained landing flaps. Exported to several US allies, P-26s were still flying when America entered the war in 1941, and the last pair was not retired, in favour of P-51 Mustangs, until 1956. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
p-26a_34: This Peashooter carries the markings of the Philippine Army Air Corps, whose 6th Pursuit Squadron under Captain Jesús Villamor flew P-26s against far superior Zeros after the Japanese invasion in December 1941, winning some fights before the last four were burned during the retreat. In the game it has two 7.62 mm Brownings in place of the 12.7 mm M2 found on the American version. It sits between two worlds: quicker than biplanes but unable to out-turn them, and handier than most monoplanes but slower than them. It arrived in Update 1.43.
p-26a_34_m2: The P-26A was the production version of Boeing's XP-936, ordered in 1933 in a batch of more than 100 and powered by a supercharged Pratt & Whitney R-1340-27 Wasp of around 500 hp, later raised to 600 hp. This version's distinguishing feature in the game is a 12.7 mm machine gun in place of a 7.62 mm one, hitting harder, reaching further and overheating more slowly. It turns tightly for a monoplane, though biplanes still turn tighter, and it has the landing flaps later added to all P-26s. It has been available since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
p-26b_35: One of Boeing's first monoplanes, the all-metal P-26 used the R-1340 Wasp radial, and the P-26B introduced a fuel-injected version plus landing flaps that cut its risky landing speed from about 131 km/h to 117 km/h. In the game its top speed of roughly 377 km/h is enough to leave some biplanes behind, though newer monoplanes catch it easily, and it turns respectably without matching biplanes. Two nose-mounted 7.62 mm guns and a pair of 100 lb bombs make up its armament, and despite its age it can hold its own against somewhat newer aircraft. It dates from the open beta, before Update 1.27.
p-36a: Curtiss built the P-36 Hawk as a private venture with an all-metal structure, enclosed cockpit and retractable undercarriage; it first flew in 1935, and though outdated in US service by 1939 it sold well abroad as the Hawk 75, flying for both Allied and Axis air arms. The P-36A, the first production model, saw its only American combat at Pearl Harbor, where a few took on Zeros; 215 were built. In the game it is nimble for an early monoplane and faster than most biplanes, and its nose-mounted 12.7 mm and 7.62 mm guns, while modest, are enough for the lightly built aircraft it usually meets. It arrived in Update 1.31.
p-36a_rasmussen: This P-36A wears the markings of Philip Rasmussen, who on 7 December 1941 ran to the airfield at Pearl Harbor still in his pyjamas, took off in one of the few intact P-36As and shot down an A6M2 despite a jammed .30 cal gun, then brought his badly damaged aircraft home without brakes, rudder or tailwheel, earning the Silver Star. It flies exactly like the standard P-36A: agile for an early monoplane, quicker than most biplanes and armed with a 12.7 mm and a 7.62 mm gun that are adequate against lightly built opponents. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
p-36c: Judged under-gunned even before it entered service, the P-36A was given a pair of .30 cal wing guns to become the P-36C, but with the type already outdated, only 30 were built and they were relegated to training. It keeps the P-36A's good agility and reasonable speed and can out-turn contemporaries such as the Bf 109 and I-16. The extra guns help against lightly built biplanes and early monoplanes, but sturdier, more modern fighters shrug off its fire, and with no protection of its own it suffers badly against them. It arrived in Update 1.31.
p-36c_rb: Curtiss's Hawk 75 paired an all-metal monoplane layout and a 900 hp radial with very low wing loading, making it an outstanding turner, though it had no supercharger and at first lacked cockpit armour and self-sealing tanks; Finnish pilots, who called it "Sussu", scored 190.3 victories with it. This P-36C, in a crying-seal camouflage, came in Update "Sky Guardians" for players using YouTuber TheRussianBadger's affiliate link. Much like mid-tier Japanese fighters, it wins by turning tightly and handling well at low speed rather than through climb or speed. One .50 cal and three .30 cal guns handle fighters but struggle with bombers, and the pilot is poorly protected.
p-36g: Ordered by Norway as the Hawk 75A-8, with a 1,200 hp Wright Cyclone and two 12.7 mm plus four 7.62 mm guns, these aircraft were stranded by the German invasion of 1940; 30 went to the exiled Norwegians' "Little Norway" camp in Canada, then to the USAAF as the P-36G and on to Peru in 1943. In the game it is the best-armed P-36, with handling that can match Bf 109s and Hurricanes but no gain in top speed, so most opponents can run it down. Extra armour and deleted wing tanks help against rifle-calibre fire, but heavy machine guns and cannon still tear it apart. It arrived in Update 1.35.
p-38e: First of the Lightnings in the game, the P-38E is a twin-engined fighter added in Update 1.53 "Firestorm". It usually starts in the air as an interceptor, so it often begins a fight level with or above the enemy. Speed and the ability to hold energy are its main weapons, which suits boom-and-zoom and energy fighting, and although single-engined fighters will out-turn it, it is more agile than its size suggests and can hold its own when pressed.
p-38g: A small step on from the P-38F, the P-38G ran its Allison engines at slightly higher boost and had better radios, though cooling problems capped power at altitude; more than 1,000 were built, many as unarmed F-5A camera aircraft. In the game it is a clear improvement on the earlier P-38, with stronger engines, a lighter airframe and rockets, and its excellent climb and concentrated nose guns make it a strong fighter. Like other early Lightnings it has no dive brakes, so compressibility in steep dives remains a hazard. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
p-38g_metal: The XP-38G was the prototype for the P-38G, the Lightning model that brought a strengthened centre wing, provision for drop tanks and more powerful engines; deliveries began in June 1942 and 1,082 P-38Gs were built. In the game it is identical to the P-38G-1 apart from its bare polished-aluminium finish, as pre-production aircraft went unpainted. It is best flown on speed and energy: quick down low and holding its performance at height better than many rivals, it does especially well in battles that start above 5,000 m, and careful use of combat flaps lets it turn with some fighters. It has been available since the open beta.
p-38j: The P-38J reworked the Lightning's engine nacelles and cooling, including a new intercooler and better turbocharger control, so the same engines as the P-38H could run about 13% harder at altitude. In the game an air spawn and good climb, best at about 275 km/h IAS, let it get above many opponents, and it carries the usual nose battery of one 20 mm cannon and four 12.7 mm guns. Although rated to 790 km/h, it still suffers from compressibility, which can spoil its aim or stop it pulling out of a dive. Bombs and rockets are available, but it is better spent hunting aircraft; it arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
p-38j_marge: This P-38J-15 carries the colours of Richard Bong, the top-scoring American ace, credited with 40 victories in the Lightning; it was a reward from the 2016 "Chronicles of World War II" event during Update 1.57 "Battle March". It reaches about 694 km/h, with an overspeed warning at 740 km/h, and carries a 20 mm AN/M2 cannon and four 12.7 mm Brownings in the nose. Modifications add rockets or bombs, letting it attack ground targets as well as aircraft.
p-38k: The P-38K put V-1710-75/77 engines of well over 1,600 hp and improved propellers into a P-38G airframe, and 1943 tests showed it out-climbing the P-47D and P-51B; retooling for the new engines would have taken too long, so only one prototype was built. Sold as a premium pack since Update 1.53 "Firestorm", and offered in sales and events ever since, it has the best flight performance of any Lightning in the game. Its armament is the usual 20 mm cannon and four 12.7 mm guns in the nose, with no bombs or rockets, which makes it purely, and very capably, an air-to-air fighter.
p-38l: Last of the researchable American Lightnings, the P-38L-5-LO arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm". Its key improvement over the P-38J-15 is dive brakes, which make recovering from a high-speed dive far easier than in earlier models, and the "New Boosters" modification sharpens its roll rate considerably. Fast, quick to climb, reasonably agile and heavily armed, it is at its best as an air-superiority fighter using boom-and-zoom attacks.
p-38l_1_china_rocaf: This P-38L wears Nationalist Chinese markings, although the Lightnings Nationalist China actually flew were mostly unarmed reconnaissance versions; in 1950 a Nationalist pilot lost his life after detecting MiG-15s, and the type was phased out by 1953 in favour of US-supplied jets. In the Chinese tree it climbs very well for its size and hits extremely hard. With enemies often at the same height, it does best by planning ahead, energy-fighting opponents who have given up their altitude or taking on heavy fighters, and using its speed to leave a melee before its large airframe soaks up hits. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
p-39k_1: Bell's Airacobra had tricycle landing gear and its engine behind the cockpit; the P-39K-1, of which 210 were built, added a stronger nose gear leg to the P-39D-2, and while poor altitude performance disappointed the British, the type thrived with Soviet pilots. In the game it is quick both level and diving, can turn with most opponents if it uses its flaps well, many Japanese and British fighters excepted, and has the firepower and protection to tackle bigger aircraft. Against that, the engine fades at altitude, the 37 mm trajectory takes practice and the fuel tanks are exposed; it has been in the Soviet tree since the open beta.
p-39n: The P-39N was the first Airacobra built in large numbers, 2,095 of them in 1942-43, with an Allison V-1710-85 and a 3.15 m Aeroproducts three-blade propeller. Many went to the Soviet Union, where it excelled as a frontline fighter, while other Allies, put off by its poor high-altitude performance, mostly used it for ground attack. In the game it is responsive and well balanced, quick and an excellent climber, but it bleeds energy in long turns, overheats badly and weakens at altitude, and its 37 mm cannon is demanding, with heavy shell drop, slow fire and little ammunition. It has been in the game since the open beta.
p-39n_su: This Airacobra is painted as the mount of Aleksandr Pokryshkin, the 16th Guards Fighter Regiment ace who won the bulk of his air victories flying Lend-Lease P-39s. Unlike the standard P-39N-0 it has no wing-mounted .30 cal guns, which improves its overall performance at almost no cost. Agile enough to turn away from several pursuers, it relies on its accurate nose-mounted 37 mm M4 cannon and 12.7 mm Brownings, which reward the careful trigger discipline many Soviet fighters demand, and it is most comfortable at low and medium altitude. Added in Update 1.31, it returns to the store each year around Pokryshkin's birthday.
p-39q_15: The Q series was the last and most numerous Airacobra, with 4,905 built up to August 1944, 3,291 of them for the Soviet Union; it swapped the four wing rifle-calibre guns for two heavy machine guns, and the Q-15 added an automatic propeller governor that eased handling in combat. Soviet pilots valued its radio, view, firepower and tricycle gear. Quick, responsive and a decent climber in the game, it is undone in long turning fights, where it sheds energy, and at altitude, where the engine fades; it also runs hot, and the 37 mm cannon's drop, slow fire and few shells make it demanding. It dates from the open beta.
p-39q_25_france: The P-39Q-25 belonged to the final Airacobra series, with two heavy machine guns replacing the earlier wing guns and, on this sub-type, a four-bladed propeller; Free French units patrolled Africa with theirs before striking ground targets and convoys across Italy and southern France, retiring them soon after the war. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season III, "Strength athletics". Nimble and quick to respond but ordinary otherwise, it has good speed and a decent climb, yet turning drains its energy, the engine overheats and loses power with height, and the 37 mm needs practice given its drop, slow fire and limited rounds.
p-39q_5: The P-39Q-5 replaces the P-39N-0's four .30 cal wing guns with a pair of .50 cal guns in underwing pods, a firepower gain paid for with extra drag and wing loading and a lower top speed. Like other Airacobras it lacks the altitude performance to chase high bombers, and the 37 mm M4's arcing shells and slow rate of fire make head-on passes a poor bet. It is happiest as a low-level fighter, escorting friendly attackers and low-flying bombers or picking off the enemy's. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
p-400: The P-400 was the export Airacobra built for Britain, carrying a 20 mm Hispano in place of the usual 37 mm; the RAF, unimpressed by its climb and altitude performance, used only 80 and passed 200 to the USSR, and the US kept another 200 after Pearl Harbor. In the game it is fastest at about 2,400 m and quick at low to medium height, turning well at speed but growing unstable when slow, so fast horizontal attacks suit it better than stall fights. The 20 mm has only 60 rounds, but two .50 cal and four .30 cal guns keep it dangerous afterwards. It arrived in Update 1.37.
p-40c: The P-40C looks almost exactly like the later P-40E, but its .50 cal machine guns sit in the nose, giving a tighter cone of fire than other American fighters it meets. Added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance", it was a reward from the 2017 "Festive Quest" event and was later offered in the Warbond shop from Battle Pass Season I through Season IV, "Fearless Voltigeur".
p-40c_china: An export Warhawk close to the P-40C, the H-81A-2 was flown in China by the American Volunteer Group, the "Flying Tigers"; pilots disliked its lack of drop tanks and bomb racks, its leak- and overheat-prone engine, missing radios and poor climb, but its sturdy structure protected them and survived crash landings. In the game its nose-mounted .50 cal guns give a tight cone of fire that keeps it competitive with similar fighters. Poor high-altitude performance and a mediocre climb mean it still needs to gain height early in a match. It arrived as a premium pack in Update 1.91 "Night Vision" and was withdrawn from sale after the 2020 May Sale.
p-40e: Part of the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27, the P-40E-1 Warhawk carries six .50 cal M2 Brownings, enough for aircraft, light pillboxes and some light tanks and AA, and it can take bombs as a capable low-tier fighter-bomber. Its engine weakens above roughly 3,000 m, so it fights best at medium height or lower, where its straight-line speed outpaces Bf 109s, A6Ms and upgraded biplanes. It wins by speed and energy rather than turning: at high speed it can out-turn some early Bf 109s and Hurricanes, but Zeros, He 112s, Spitfires and early Soviet fighters will all beat it in a turn.
p-40e_china: Apart from its emerald green camouflage, China's P-40E-1 is the same aircraft as the American version, added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision" as the successor to the P-66 in the Chinese tree. Like the P-66 it is well armed and well protected but only average in the air. Its six 12.7 mm M2 Brownings, standard for US fighters, hit hard even with early-war ammunition, and bombs are available for ground targets. Contemporary fighters often outperform it, so it rewards a careful pilot rather than a reckless one.
p-40e_td: Handed out in Update "New Power" to viewers of War Thunder streams on Twitch, along with a unique skin, the P-40E-1 TD is otherwise the standard Warhawk. Six .50 cal Brownings deal with aircraft, light fortifications and some light vehicles, and bombs turn it into a useful low-tier fighter-bomber. It belongs at medium altitude or below, where its engine performs and its level speed outruns Bf 109s and Zeros, and it should fight with energy and speed, since Spitfires, Zeros, He 112s and early Soviet fighters all out-turn it.
p-40e_ussr: The P-40E-1 in Soviet markings is a premium Kittyhawk that has been in the game since the open beta. Its six 12.7 mm Brownings carry plenty of ammunition and work against ground targets too, though bombs are best left off so it stays nimble for air combat. Like other P-40s it prefers medium and low altitude, as the engine fades higher up, and its main asset is level speed, enough to catch Bf 109 E-3s, which still out-climb it, and Zeros. A good pattern is to run a target down, zoom up a few hundred metres and dive back in; lightly armoured Zeros can even be met head-on.
p-40f-5_france_ep: The P-40F swapped the Allison for a Merlin of about 1,300 hp, losing the scoop on top of the nose and gaining a longer fuselage for stability; it was also the model that brought the "Warhawk" name. This one is named after GC 2/4 La Fayette, the Free French squadron that flew them in North Africa. Even with the Merlin it fights best low down, and it grows heavy at high speed, making aiming difficult, but its 819 km/h limit lets it dive out of trouble. Six 12.7 mm guns give solid firepower, held back only by early-war belts; it is a premium added in Update "Raining Fire".
p-40f_10: To cure the Allison engine's weakness at height, a Merlin went into a P-40D in 1941, leading to the P-40F, which used the Packard-built version of about 1,300 hp for better altitude performance, range and all-round speed; more than 1,300 were built, some for the RAF. In the game that engine lets it fight higher up than earlier Warhawks, while it otherwise keeps their familiar traits. It is easy to spot by the missing intake on top of the nose and the longer fuselage added to cope with the Merlin's torque. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
p-43a-1: Seversky's P-43 Lancer grew out of the P-35 and paved the way for the P-47; its belly-mounted turbo-supercharger and good oxygen system made it a strong high-altitude performer in 1940, yet the Army judged it obsolete and used it for training, while 125 sent to China proved less survivable than the P-40. In the game it is a heavy fighter that should climb first, choose its targets and attack in diving passes, zooming away afterwards rather than turning back to finish a damaged enemy, which wastes its energy; Japanese fighters will out-turn it. It came in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica" and was an event reward in 2017 and 2018.
p-47d: Complaints about the razorback Thunderbolt's restricted view led to a 1943 trial with a Typhoon bubble canopy, and the Farmingdale-built P-47D-25 followed with that canopy, a paddle-blade propeller, extra fuel and an R-2800-59 producing over 2,000 hp with water injection; after the war many P-47Ds went to countries such as Chile and Iran. In the game the heavy "Jug" reaches about 700 km/h and tolerates dives to 885 km/h, and its good control at speed and eight long-reaching M2 Brownings suit boom-and-zoom. Plenty of ammunition plus bombs and rockets also make it a solid ground attacker. It has been in the game since the open beta.
p-47d-28: Too short-ranged to shepherd bombers to distant European targets, the Thunderbolt left high-altitude escort to Merlin Mustangs and found its niche attacking small targets such as bridges, a job its size and toughness suited. The D-28 differs from the D-25 mainly in its Curtiss Electric propeller, which performs almost exactly like the D-25's Hamilton Standard, and in offering M10 bazooka tubes, though HVAR rockets do far more damage. In the air it is strictly a boom-and-zoom aircraft that climbs away after a missed pass, and its radial engine and eight .50 cals make head-ons reasonable. It arrived in Update 1.33.
p-47d_16_re_germany: The P-47D-16-RE was a Farmingdale-built Thunderbolt with minor fuel-system changes, of which 254 were made; on 7 November 1943 William Roach was forced to put one down on a German airfield, where it was given German markings as T9+LK and, like other captured P-47s, used for testing, training and propaganda until American troops retook it. In the German tree it has the heavy guns, top speed, high-speed handling and dive limit that make boom-and-zoom its natural style. It is big, slow to climb and leaves the pilot almost unprotected, and most fighters beat it in a turning fight. It arrived in Update 2.1 "New Power".
p-47d_22_re: Among the last razorback Thunderbolts, the P-47D-22-RE paired a water-injected R-2800-63 with a huge 3.9 m Hamilton Standard propeller that cleared the ground by just 15 cm but brought a big gain in climb; the D-23-RA was the same aircraft with a Curtiss Electric propeller. In the game the razorback spine steadies it at speed but blocks the rear view, and its great weight means a poor climb and energy gone after a few hard turns, so turning fights are a last resort. Its ground-attack choices are narrower than later Thunderbolts', but bombs alone or bombs with rockets are available; it arrived in Update "Raining Fire".
p-47d_22_re_france: This Thunderbolt represents serial 42-26157, the 619th P-47D-22-RE built, which served the Free French with GC II/3 "Dauphiné" late in the war; beyond a few photos and drawings, little is known of its career. Added in Update "New Power", it brings the P-47D's heavy firepower and strong engine, and although it is arguably too heavy for long turning or energy fights, its large ammunition supply gives plenty of margin for error against aircraft. A modest but useful bomb load lets it cause trouble on the ground as well, making it a versatile aircraft and a good stepping stone for players.
p-47d_23_ra_china_rocaf: Nationalist China received 107 P-47Ds in the mid-1940s, among them seven D-23-RAs handed over in April 1945, though little is recorded of what they did; razorback Thunderbolts of the US 14th Air Force had already been escorting bombers and transports in China. Added in Update "New Power" alongside razorback P-47Ds in other trees, it keeps the framed canopy used before the D-25 and a strong engine. Its payload trails later Thunderbolts, but its firepower is ample for energy-fighting enemy aircraft or striking ground targets as a multirole.
p-47d_30_china: Once the war was over, the Nationalist air force inherited 102 Thunderbolts from the US 14th Air Force, later adding around 250 F-47Ns; they fought in the Civil War, then formed the core of Taiwan's fighter arm until 1957. In the Chinese tree the P-47D-30 is built for fast hit-and-run attacks: it is quick, handles well at high speed, survives very fast dives and carries a heavy gun battery. A large load of bombs and rockets makes it a handy ground attacker as well, though its weight shows in a poor climb. It arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
p-47d_30_italy: Italy, a founding NATO member in 1949, received around 100 surplus P-47s from the US under the Mutual Defense programme to rebuild its air force; the D-30 was essentially a D-28 with small improvements and dive brakes. In the game water injection pushes it to about 714 km/h, and while it feels sluggish, that speed and its control at high speed make it dangerous to enemy fighters. A wide choice of ground-attack loadouts handles tanks and pillboxes, and some 34 seconds of firing time leaves plenty of ammunition for anti-aircraft guns and other soft targets. It arrived in Update "Sky Guardians".
p-47d_luftwaffe: Allied fighters sometimes came down on the wrong side of the lines after damage or navigation errors, and at least three P-47Ds fell into German hands this way, to be used for mock combat, comparative tests and propaganda. This version has a bubble canopy and slightly different performance from the razorback P-47D-16-RE in the same tree. It suits boom-and-zoom, with strong guns, good top speed, sure handling at speed and a high dive limit, but its size, weak climb and nearly unarmoured cockpit count against it, and most fighters beat it in a dogfight. It has been in the game since the open beta.
p-47d_ussr: The Soviet P-47D-27 is a Lend-Lease Thunderbolt that differs from the American D-25 mainly in its camouflage and in carrying Soviet FAB bombs measured in kilograms instead of American AN-M bombs. Eight 12.7 mm Brownings shred wings and set fuel tanks alight, and good energy retention makes it a strong boom-and-zoom fighter once it has altitude, which, given its slow initial climb, is best gained by climbing away from the fight at the start. Up to 1,250 kg of ordnance makes it a capable attacker, though HVAR rockets were not part of the Lend-Lease supply and are unavailable. It is a premium added in Update 1.43.
p-47m-1-re: This P-47M wears the "Ugly Duckling" markings of George Bostwick of the 56th Fighter Group, who scored eight confirmed air victories, including a rare Me 262 kill near Cologne in March 1945, and went on to command the 63rd Fighter Squadron. Sold as a premium pack from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it is the fastest Thunderbolt in the game, and its unmatched engine power helps it climb quickly or escape bad situations. It is also the only P-47 with underwing dive brakes, useful because the controls stiffen beyond about 700 km/h. Withdrawn after the 2020 May Sale, it has since returned for American-themed events.
p-47m-1-re_boxted: Lanovski's P-47M-1-RE is a premium gift added in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea", painted in the scheme of Witold Łanowski, a Polish pilot serving with the US Army Air Forces' 61st Fighter Squadron. It has only been sold for Golden Eagles during Polish-themed events, such as those marking Poland's independence, Constitution Day and Armed Forces Day, between 2018 and 2023.
p-47n-15: The P-47N-15 is a Thunderbolt refined for boom-and-zoom fighting, able to approach 800 km/h with an airframe built to cope, and its eight .50 cal Brownings make each pass very dangerous. Its redesigned wing has clipped tips that raise level speed and give a quicker, more controllable roll, yet adds area overall, which noticeably improves pitch response. The wing also made room for a wider undercarriage and extra fuel for range, and the added weight costs it climb rate. It arrived in Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
p-51_a-36: With no money for new fighters in 1942 but funds available for attack aircraft, North American kept its Mustang line running by turning the design into the A-36A dive bomber, with stronger wings, bomb racks and dive brakes; 500 were built and served in the Mediterranean and the China-Burma-India theatre. Its Allison V-1710-87 is weak at altitude but works well low down, and the dive brakes hold dives to around 630 km/h, leaving energy to zoom back up or escape interceptors. After bombing it becomes a strafer, with six 12.7 mm guns plus four more in optional pods for soft targets and aircraft. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
p-51_mk1a_usaaf: This early Mustang pairs the Allison engine with four 20 mm Hispano Mk.II cannons, its standout feature, though their 500 rounds call for disciplined shooting. It climbs poorly and turns only averagely, but dives very fast and holds energy well, so boom-and-zoom is the way to fly it. Once upgraded, the engine is hard to overheat even on WEP, although heat builds if it runs at full power for long, and well-used flaps can keep it alive in turning fights, sometimes even against Soviet fighters. Its quick-killing cannons suit newcomers to Realistic Battles; it arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
p-51a_tl: The P-51A gave the early Mustang the uprated Allison V-1710-81 of up to 1,200 hp, with a supercharger that held more of that power at altitude, and a larger propeller, making it one of the fastest fighters of its day; its four 12.7 mm wing guns jammed often, and over 1,500 were built before the Merlin arrived. In the game it is a very capable boom-and-zoom fighter that dives superbly, though compressibility means steep dives near the ground need care, and dogfights are best avoided unless the opponent is badly placed. It was a rare reward from the 2015 Thunder League, added in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
p-51b: The Mustang Mk IA is a premium British fighter that has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27. Mechanically it matches the American P-51: an Allison engine and a quartet of wing-mounted 20 mm cannons. What sets it apart is its appearance: a two-tone desert camouflage over a light blue underside, with RAF roundels on the wings and fuselage and a red, white and blue fin flash.
p-51b_7_sweden: J26 David was a P-51B-7 that ran low on fuel and came down in Sweden during early 1944; after Sweden bought it and other Mustangs from the US, it joined the Swedish Air Force in spring 1945, saw no combat and was probably scrapped with the other P-51Bs in the late 1940s. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season 11, "Her Majesty's Hussar". Compared with the J26 in the research tree it has fewer machine guns and a different cockpit but can carry two bombs of up to 500 lb, leaving a fast, agile fighter whose firepower is on the light side.
p-51c-10-nt: Packard's licence-built Merlin, the V-1650, with its two-speed, two-stage supercharger, first reached production Mustangs in the P-51B and near-identical P-51C, transforming their performance at height; this one carries the default markings of the 332nd Fighter Group, the African-American "Red Tails". In the game it flies like the Merlin-engined P-51D-5 and D-20-NA and edges them in some areas. Its weak point is armament: only four wing-mounted M2 Brownings, helped somewhat by late-war belts, and unremarkable suspended ordnance. It came in Update "Raining Fire" and is a good primer for later American piston fighters.
p-51c-10_france: The F-6C was a P-51C, the first Merlin-powered Mustang model, fitted with two reconnaissance cameras; the Merlin and a strengthened airframe put it on terms with the Fw 190 and Bf 109, and France used F-6Cs to photograph Germany late in the war. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season VII, "Armoured Elephant", during Update "Wind of Change". Far faster and a much better climber than Allison Mustangs, it also has a roomier canopy with a better view. It keeps the usual four 12.7 mm wing guns but carries no bombs or rockets, and like other P-51s it relies on boom-and-zoom rather than dogfighting.
p-51c-11-nt_china: The Dallas-built counterpart of the Inglewood P-51B, the P-51C was produced from summer 1943 to September 1944, the C-11 using the high-altitude Packard V-1650-7. China's Chinese-American Composite Wing began receiving Mustangs in November 1944 to replace its outclassed P-40s, starting with B and C models before Ds and Ks arrived, and they later fought in the Civil War. A reward in Battle Pass Season 15, "Northern King", it is fast and agile, but four M2 Brownings demand good positioning and sustained bursts, and later Mustangs beat it for firepower and, in Simulator Battles, cockpit view.
p-51c-11-nt_japan: Named "Evalina" by 1st Lt. Oliver E. Strawbridge after his girlfriend, this P-51C made a forced landing on 16 January 1945 and was captured; with hinomaru painted over its stars, it was shipped to Japan, where the Army studied it and flew it in mock combat almost until the war ended. Added in Update "Red Skies", it is the American P-51C-10 without bombs, and as a 1945 capture it gets late-war .50 cal belts, including incendiary AP-I/T. Japanese pilots used to turning fighters must adapt to its style: dive in fast, hit hard with ample ammunition, then break off and climb back up.
p-51d-10: Painted as the aircraft of Ray S. Wetmore, an American ace credited with 21 German aircraft, this P-51D-10 differs from the D-5 only in having a dorsal fin on its tail, the first Mustang model to carry one. First sold as the "Daddy's Girl" premium pack in the "Weapons of Victory" update, it has since appeared on and off through Warbonds, Steam and seasonal store sales. Its speed and firepower suit boom-and-zoom attacks and bomber interception, and it performs better than expected as a light attacker.
